thread:
Grace Kim: Dropping early numbers from the tier sweep on `llama-3-70b-instruct` (H100-80GB, runtime-1.21.0-rc2). This is *not* final, but directional.

Workload: chat, non-streaming, 512 tok prompt / 256 tok gen, concurrency=32, 10 min steady-state after warmup.

```
Tier           max_queue_delay  max_batch_tokens  p95 (ms)  p99 (ms)  req/s   tok/s    est $ / 1M tok
fast           2ms              4096              820       1080      5.8     1480     0.92
standard       6ms              6144              900       1220      6.5     1670     0.83
cost_efficient 14ms             8192              1090      1510      7.6     1950     0.70
```

So cost_efficient is ~24–25% cheaper vs fast on this shape, but p95 +270ms (and p99 looks a bit gnarly). Standard is ~10% cheaper w/ +80ms p95.

Benchmark-lab report: https://benchmark-lab/redwood/runs/2025-03-03/llama3-70b-tier-sweep (internal)

Questions:
1) are we comfortable w/ that p95 delta for cost_efficient as the *default* for anyone who opts in?
2) I didn’t run streaming yet (separate run queued).

:bar_chart: :eyes:

Sofia Ivanova: thanks Grace. those numbers match my intuition (cost tier buys throughput via queueing). the p99 jump is the thing that’ll page SRE if customers set tight timeouts.

Can you share queue delay histos? Are we seeing long tail in `queue_wait_ms` or decode contention?

Marcus Reed: +1, would love to see stage breakdown. In my local run the p95 increase was mostly queue wait once we crossed ~6ms and started forming bigger prefills.

Also what was `prefill_weight:decode_weight` for each tier in that run? (I assume default mapping.)

Grace Kim: yep default mapping from PR_18435.

Queue wait summary (from the run logs):
- fast: queue_wait_ms p95 ~1.6ms, p99 ~2.3ms
- standard: queue_wait_ms p95 ~4.8ms, p99 ~7.2ms
- cost_efficient: queue_wait_ms p95 ~11.9ms, p99 ~19.5ms

Decode looks a little spikier in cost_efficient too (more active sequences per cycle).

Omar El-Sayed: That p99 queue wait in cost_efficient is actually lower than I feared. The bigger hit might be KV cache pressure -> more evictions -> re-prefill work? Did we see `kv_cache_evict_bytes` bump?

Grace Kim: I didn’t pull KV metrics yet. I can add them to the next report; this run only had the default perf CSV + the queue delay histogram.

Yuki Sato: another axis: GPU util. If cost_efficient is driving util into the high 90s we’ll see more tail from any microbursts.

Do we know what util was?

Grace Kim: avg SM util:
- fast ~71%
- standard ~78%
- cost_efficient ~86%

Memory util stayed ~63–66% (no OOMs).

Julian Moore: fwiw this matches the tracing I saw earlier: once we let queue delay go >10ms, we get “fatter” batches, but any jitter on arrival patterns produces occasional queue_wait outliers that cascade into end-to-end.

We might want a guardrail: cap queue_wait based on observed concurrency / arrival rate (or at least don’t let it hit 14ms when concurrency < X).

Sofia Ivanova: agree. also reminder: cost_efficient tier isn’t for *all* use-cases. It’s for batch-y backends and async-ish routes.

But we should still define the contract clearly. Product keeps asking if it’s “safe” for general use. IMO: safe yes, but only if customers accept higher p95/p99 and set timeouts accordingly.

Sean Gallagher: jumping in w/ SRE hat. for Hosted, we’re going to get customers w/ 1–2s app timeouts and no retries. if cost_efficient p99 is 1.5s on this workload, they’ll feel it.

Two things I’d want before we recommend:
1) explicit guidance on timeout/retry settings per tier
2) clear auto-rollback triggers if timeouts / cancellations jump

Also: do we have `timeout_rate` / `client_cancel_rate` in this run?

Grace Kim: no client cancels in the harness, so we don’t see real cancel behavior here. But server-side timeouts were 0 in all tiers.

Marcus Reed: for (1) in Grace’s question: I don’t think cost_efficient should be “recommended” as default for interactive chat. Standard seems reasonable.

Cost tier should be opt-in w/ a big warning + maybe we default it only for non-streaming + higher concurrency routes (embeddings-ish, rerank, batch jobs). But PM said “three tiers across all routes”, so we need a policy.

Omar El-Sayed: another thought: those numbers are for 512/256. if we run long prefill (e.g., 4k prompt) the cost tier might be worse because queueing + prefill blocking. That’s where we need workload-aware logic.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. workload-aware selection is the entire point. Grace’s numbers are still useful: they show the cost/latency frontier.

Action items?
- Grace: run streaming for same model, concurrency 32 and 64? cadence check too.
- Marcus/Omar: can we extract per-stage breakdown (queue/prefill/decode) into the perf report template?
- Julian: propose a “max effective queue delay” clamp based on observed arrival rate (even if heuristic).

Grace Kim: ack. I’ll queue streaming run now. Also will rerun cost_efficient with queue_delay 10ms (instead of 14ms) to see if we get most of the savings w/ less p95 pain.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to trying 10ms. If we can keep cost tier p99 < ~1.3s on this shape it’s easier to message.

Yuki Sato: please include A100-80GB too when you get a sec. H100 looks great but we have a lot of A100 Dedicated customers.

Grace Kim: will do. A100 runs take longer but I’ll at least do standard vs cost_efficient to start.

Julian Moore: reaction: :thumbsup: to the 10ms experiment. also if we can add a metric to track “formed batch tokens vs target cap” per tier, we can see if we’re hitting diminishing returns.

Sofia Ivanova: cool. please drop results back here when streaming run is done. and let’s sync w/ Aditya later this week with a crisp “what you get / what you pay” summary.

Grace Kim: sounds good. I’ll post an update tomorrow after the overnight jobs finish.
